nodes.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker state: `processMSG` decodes the service NodeId from the attacker-controlled OPC UA `MSG` body into `requestTypeId`, creating the dispatch key that drives the message into AddNodes handling.

Root cause. After `UA_Nodestore_insert` has transferred ownership of the new node into the nodestore, `Operation_addNode_begin` still passes the raw `UA_Node *node` and the callback-selected item's parent/reference/type data into `addParentAndTypeRef` without acquiring a nodestore reference. If that helper deletes the node on an error path, the caller's `node` alias becomes dangling but is still reused in the caller's own error cleanup.
MSAN crash site. During the second delete of the already freed nodestore entry, cleanup reaches `NodeId_deleteMembers` and branches on the freed `nodeId.identifierType` field.

nodes.state: When addParentAndTypeRef returns an error, Operation_addNode_begin still passes the same raw `node` pointer to UA_Nodestore_delete(server, node) even though deleteNodeOperation already released and freed that nodestore entry.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records helper_delete_release.released_node_ptr == caller_cleanup_delete.cleanup_delete_arg.
